family: Aftermarket 1-DIN with a large dot-matrix display
examples: Sony CDX-GT with the FL dot matrix
one_liner: The best donor there is, and the cheapest way to a deck that does not look home-made.

price.v: £8–20 spares-or-repair; £30–60 working, which you do not need
price.why: Search “spares or repair”, “no CD”, “display dead”, “untested”. You are buying the box and the face.

window_w_mm.why: Varies by model. Measure with calipers.

chassis.why: Gives you the box, and usually the cage and trim ring too.

cage_included.v: often — pay a little more for one that has it
cage_included.why: A new cage is £8–15, so a £15 unit with one beats a £8 without.

buttons.v: typically 8–14 on a flexi matrix, plus a rotary knob
buttons.why: More than enough for the six-button ladder, with spares.

knob.v: rotary volume, usually an encoder or a pot with a detent feel
knob.why: Reuse the KNOB and fit your own EC11 behind it — the original's electrical type does not matter, only its shaft and cap do.

display_tech.v: LCD or VFD depending on model
display_tech.why: ⚠️ If it is a VFD, its power board makes tens of volts and holds them after power-off. See the hazards.

why: The window is already a wide letterbox of roughly the right size, in roughly the right place, and usually already amber on black — which is exactly what the deck draws.
They were made in enormous numbers and are worthless to everybody else once the CD mechanism jams, which is what makes them cheap.
The fascia has enough buttons to fill the ladder without drilling.

⚠️ One caution that applies to the whole family: several of these have a native display of 128×32, which is HALF the deck's 256×64 across. The physical window is usually close to right because our panel has a finer pitch — but 'usually close' is not 'measured', and this is the family where a few millimetres decides it.
watch_out: Motorised or flip-out fascias. The mechanism eats depth, it is fragile, and it is one more thing to defeat. Buy a fixed face.
Models where the CD slot dominates the front — the window is small and high, and the deck's panel wants the middle.
⚠️ VFD models: the inverter board. Discharge it and bin it.
steps: Take the fascia off FIRST, before any screws. Clips, not fasteners, and thirty years old. It is the part you cannot replace.
Unscrew the top and bottom covers and keep every screw — they are the right length for this chassis and nothing in your box will be.
Lift the whole internal assembly out before cutting anything, so you can see what holds what.
Bin the CD mechanism, the amplifier board and the main PCB. Discharge the large electrolytics first.
Keep the flexi from the button panel attached to the fascia and cut it free of the main board — you want the switches, not the matrix.
Lift the switch commons and wire each switch to its ladder resistor. Six buttons, six resistors, one wire to the deck.
Dry-fit the deck's panel behind the window before bonding anything, and check the lit area is centred in the aperture rather than in the fascia.

models.name: Pioneer DEH-P9000R
models.note: The first car-audio OEL display Pioneer ever shipped, and the start of the whole look this project is chasing. Sought after, so not the cheapest — but the fascia is exactly right.

models.name: Pioneer MEH-P9000R
models.note: The MiniDisc sibling of the DEH-P9000R with the same face. MiniDisc is worthless to everybody, which makes this the cheap way to that fascia.

models.name: Pioneer DEH-P9100R
models.note: Second-generation OEL. Same idea, easier to find than the 9000R.

models.name: Pioneer MEH-P9100R
models.note: Again the MiniDisc twin — same fascia, a fraction of the price.

models.name: Pioneer DEH-P6600
models.display: OEL dot matrix, 128×32 + 24×32, blue and white
models.note: ⚠️ The most useful model here because its display resolution is published. 128×32 is HALF the deck's 256×64 across — the window is sized for a coarser display, so measure before assuming the panel drops in. See the note under the drawing.

models.name: Pioneer DEH-P6800MP
models.note: Common, cheap, and the right shape. A good default if you see one.

models.name: Pioneer DEH-P6300
models.note: Screensavers on the original, which tells you the window is generous — nobody animates a two-line display.

models.name: Pioneer DEH-P9400MP
models.display: OEL, user-loadable animation via PC Link
models.note: Pioneer let owners upload their own animations to this one. That means the window was made to be looked at, which is exactly what you want.

models.name: Pioneer DEH-P7800MP
models.note: A colour OEL. The deck's panel is monochrome, so you are buying the window and the face, not the technology — but both are excellent.

models.name: Pioneer DEH-P9600MP
models.note: ⚠️ Dual-faceplate design. More mechanism than you need and more to defeat. Buy one only if it is cheap.

models.name: Pioneer DEH-P85BT
models.note: ⚠️ AVOID for this build. Motorised faceplate: the mechanism eats depth, it is fragile, and it is one more thing to work around.

models.name: Alpine CDA-9855 / CDA-9855R
models.note: Alpine's BioLite is bright and wide-angle, and the fold-down face is well made. A very good donor.

models.name: Alpine CDA-9887 / CDA-9887R
models.note: Top of Alpine's CD line at the time — the best-built fascia in this list. Priced accordingly even broken.

models.name: Sony CDX-GT700D
models.note: ⚠️ VFD. Nice window, and its power board makes tens of volts and holds them after power-off. Treat it as live. See the hazards.

models.name: Sony CDX-M9905X
models.note: Sony's flagship of the era. Big face, big window.

models.name: Clarion DXZ935
models.note: ⚠️ The two-piece panel is more mechanism than you need.

models.name: Clarion DXZ925
models.display: large display behind a motorised face
models.note: ⚠️ AVOID. Dual-action motorised face that slides down to reveal a second faceplate. Impressive, and completely wrong for this.

models.name: Kenwood KDC-716S
models.note: ⚠️ Motorised D-MASK+ faceplate that rotates 180°. The display itself is good; the mechanism is not what you want.

models.name: Blaupunkt Bremen MP76
models.note: European, common in the UK, and the Bremen fascia is a genuinely handsome thing to build into.

models.name: Blaupunkt Woodstock DAB53
models.note: Same family, often cheaper than the Bremen because the name carries less weight.

teardown.note: Clips, thirty years old. FIRST off, before any screw — it is the part you cannot replace.
Stays with the fascia. Cut it free of the main board, not off the fascia.
Usually slides off the front once the fascia is away.
Keep every screw. They are the right length for this chassis and nothing in your box will be.
⚠️ If it is a VFD, the board behind it holds tens of volts. Discharge before handling.
One sub-assembly on four screws, comes out whole. Do not power it to test the laser.
Discharge the large electrolytics, then bin. This is the stored energy in the unit.
The decoder your buttons were wired to. Cut the flexi at the board, not at the fascia.
The box. What you came for.
If it came with them. Worth £8–15 on their own.
